newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast spot prods fall after inventory rise.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast spot prods fall after inventory rise.

text.p: Wholesale spot prices for the U.S. West Coast gasoline weakened Wednesday, following reports the day before that inventories remain ample in the region, traders said.
"(Prices) are off a good half cent from yesterday," said a trader for a large independent refining company.

West Coast gasoline stocks rose 115,00 barrels for the week ended July 4, according to the American Petroleum Institute (API), disappointing traders who had gambled that high volumes of exports the last month would lower inventories a notch.
"People were expecting exports to draw a little bit more," the trader said.
At least one parcel of July CARB gasoline sold for 54.25 cents a gallon in Los Angeles Wednesday, traders said, lowering the price range a half cent from yesterday to 54/55 cents.
August barrels sold at 54.75 cents and 55 cents, reflecting the July market's current oversupply.
Some product brokers said gasoline paper trade increased Wednesday, with 55.25 cents, 55.50 cents, and 55.75 cents sold for hedging purposes.
Traders said activity picked up today, as players anticipated prices had reached their bottom and would start to climb, given usual summertime demand, which is the heaviest period for gasoline.
One refinery trader said trade increased because players were locking in their supplies for August through spot or paper deals.
Bids for low sulphur diesel fell two cents to 50 cents a gallon today, pressured down by API data showing a solid incrase in regional stocks.

Gasoline in the Bay area remained at a slight premium to Los Angeles, which is normally one to two cents higher. CARB gasoline was talked between 56 and 57 cents a gallon, or two cents higher than L.A. due to talk that another cargo of San Francisco gasoline is scheduled to ship to the Far East later this month.

Exports, about 10 cargoes since late May, have resulted from weak profits at West Coast refineries, where the cost of raw material -- crude oil -- has greatly surpassed what refiners can fetch for products.
Traders said most cargoes were sized around 245,000 barrels and are being shipped to the Far East and southeast U.S markets.
Reformulated gasoline, for sale in the metropolitan Phoenix area, was talked one cent below CARB levels,traders said.
